description:
FILED s481b (2026-09-10, Opus) from the group-B load/work probe of the
critical-infrastructure measurement (#1607).  POSIX is on the README's list.

REPRODUCER (scratch/s481b/probe-groupb-work.pl), perl 5.40.3 vs ./runpcl:

    require POSIX;
    print POSIX::floor(3.7), "\n";                          # perl 3   PCL 3
    print POSIX::strftime("%Y", 0,0,0,1,0,100), "\n";       # perl 2000
                                    # PCL: Undefined subroutine &POSIX::strftime

`lib/POSIX.pm` supplies `floor`, `ceil`, `fmod`, `pow`, `log2`, `log10`,
`strtod`, `strtol`, `strtoul`, `dup` and the `SEEK_*` / `O_*` constants, so the
module loads and the gap only shows at the call.  `strftime` is the most-used
POSIX function in real code after the constants (it is how every log line and
every date column is formatted), so it belongs in the shim.

LAYER (CLAUDE.md 9a): a module fact â `lib/POSIX.pm`, not the runtime.
`POSIX::strftime` is expressible in plain Perl over the runtime's existing
`localtime`/`gmtime` and `sprintf`, and perl's own semantics are worth copying
exactly, including that it MKTIME-normalises its arguments before formatting
(`strftime("%Y", 0,0,0,32,0,100)` is 2000-02-01, not an error) and that `%Z` /
`%z` come from the current zone.

BAR: guard rows with perl as the oracle over the common conversions (%Y %m %d
%H %M %S %j %a %b %e %F %T %s), one out-of-range field to prove the
normalisation, and one row for `mktime` if it is added with it.  A `lib/`
change owes the full sweep.


=== FOLDED INTO #1997 (s492, Fable, 2026-09-20) ===
The everyday battery (#1994) showed strftime is one name of many: `use POSIX;` exports nothing and `use POSIX qw(strftime)` dies AT THE IMPORT.  #1997 owns the whole shim surface and carries this task`s strftime bar (the mktime normalisation probe above); close this one with #1997.


=== CLOSED with #1997 (s492c, 2026-09-21) ===
POSIX::strftime ships in the rewritten lib/POSIX.pm, with the mktime
normalisation this task named (strftime("%Y-%m-%d", 0,0,0,32,0,100) is
2000-02-01) and mktime beside it.  Guard rows 3-8 of Pl/t/posix-01.t.

=== DONE (s492c) ===
CLOSED by #1997 (s492c member 2): POSIX::strftime exists, mktime-normalises
its fields over a days-from-civil computation with no Time::Local dependency,
and DIES naming any conversion it does not implement (rule 12).
subject: `POSIX::strftime` is absent from PCL's `lib/POSIX.pm` shim â `POSIX::floor` and the constants are there, so a program that loads POSIX succeeds and then dies at the one call it actually wanted.
